slides.title: Designing Social Robots for Inclusive Child Wellbeing Assessment: Insights from Communities Supporting Developmental Language Disorder and Forced Migration
slides.highlight: This research provides design recommendations for social robots to support wellbeing assessments for children with communication barriers, aligning with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Design guidelines for inclusive social robot-mediated wellbeing assessments for children with communication barriers and forced migration backgrounds.
card.key_idea: Used interdisciplinary design probes and focus groups with parents and professionals to identify ethical, interactional, and population-specific requirements for inclusive child-robot wellbeing assessments.
card.evaluation: Qualitative thematic analysis of focus group discussions with 14 stakeholders (parents and professionals) across DLD and forced migration contexts.
card.limitation: Findings are based on stakeholder perspectives rather than direct interaction data from the target children.

slides.title: TRIBE: Predicting Team Performance via Communication Behavior Ensembles
slides.tldr: PREDICTING TEAM PERFORMANCE VIA COMMUNICATION PATTERNS
slides.highlight: TRIBE identifies communication patterns that predict team performance and behavioral dynamics, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: TRIBE predicts team performance by clustering communication patterns, enabling interventions as early as 10% task completion.
card.key_idea: A domain-independent pipeline using topic modeling (LDA/NMF) and clustering (K-means/GMM) to categorize teams into performance-predictive 'behavioral tribes' based on interaction transcripts.
card.evaluation: Tested on four datasets (Minecraft, DELI, GAP); used adjusted R², ANOVA, and Cohen’s d. Results show strong predictive power in flexible task structures.
card.limitation: Predictive effectiveness depends on the degree of behavioral freedom allowed by the specific task structure.

slides.title: Dobot Launches Full-Scenario Embodied Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: The launch of a multi-functional humanoid robot for daily and professional needs is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Robot Learning from Human Demonstrations: Handwritten Alphabet Trajectories and Human-Likeness Evaluation
slides.tldr: LEARNING HUMAN-LIKE ROBOT MOTION FROM HANDWRITING DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: This work presents a framework for learning human-like robot motion through handwriting demonstrations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A framework for learning human-like robot handwriting using an extended GMM+GMR approach and a new dataset.
card.key_idea: Extends GMM+GMR by incorporating contact force and normalized time dimensions and implementing a segment-detection step to handle non-continuous, multi-stroke handwriting trajectories.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a user study (21 participants) on 52 characters; generated trajectories scored 71.50/100 for human-likeness, with 81.2% of ratings above neutral.
card.limitation: Evaluated using a simulated robot rather than physical hardware; used predefined character guidelines and linear interpolation for pen-lift transitions.

slides.title: Toward Resilient Human-AI Collaboration: A Lifecycle Taxonomy of Sociotechnical Risks and Cascading Failures
slides.tldr: SOCIOTECHNICAL RISK TAXONOMY FOR HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION
slides.highlight: This paper identifies recurring risk clusters in human-AI collaboration, such as trust miscalibration and cognitive burden, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on modeling hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: A lifecycle taxonomy of sociotechnical risks that undermine human-AI collaboration across diverse professional domains.
card.key_idea: Proposes a four-stage lifecycle (task allocation, interaction, feedback, adoption) and six cross-domain risk clusters to explain how interconnected sociotechnical failures cascade.
card.evaluation: Synthesized evidence from fragmented literature across five domains (healthcare, journalism, education, management, defense) to identify recurring failure patterns.
card.limitation: The work provides a conceptual framework and synthesis of existing literature rather than new empirical validation.

slides.title: Deep Learning for Real-Time Sound Order Recognition in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME SOUND ORDER RECOGNITION FOR HRI
slides.highlight: This research introduces a deep learning framework to recognize the temporal order of overlapping sounds, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A deep learning framework for real-time recognition of the temporal order of overlapping non-verbal sounds.
card.key_idea: A multi-branch CNN processing Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, and STFT features, utilizing an attention-based fusion mechanism to identify sound sequences.
card.evaluation: Tested on synthetic overlaps (balanced, varied-amplitude, and unseen sounds); achieved 99% accuracy for balanced and 74% for unseen data.
card.limitation: Experiments used carefully controlled synthetic overlaps, potentially limiting ecological validity in real-room environments.

slides.title: DOBOT Unveils All-Terrain Humanoid Robot LUMO
slides.tldr: ALL-TERRAIN HUMANOID ROBOT WITH VR TELEOPERATION
slides.highlight: The introduction of the LUMO all-terrain humanoid robot and its VR teleoperation capabilities is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Accelerating Human-Aware Robot Trajectory Generation via Diffusion and Consistency Distillation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for generating collision-aware robot trajectories in HRI environments using diffusion and consistency distillation. It is relevant to RwB for improving the safety and smoothness of embodied social robot interactions.

card.one_liner: Accelerates human-aware robot trajectory generation using consistency distillation of a conditional diffusion model.
card.key_idea: A diffusion model trained on RRT/RRT* data is distilled into a consistency model with joint-weighted jerk regularization and constraint-guided sampling for fast, smooth, collision-free trajectories.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via UR5 simulations (500 test scenes); results show inference time reduced from 5.7s to ~96ms with high success rates (98-100%).
card.limitation: The framework was validated only in simulation using a UR5 manipulator; real-world physical deployment is not stated.

slides.title: LiFTER: A Grounded Neuro-Symbolic Microscope for Continuous-Time Dynamic Graph Forecasting
slides.highlight: LiFTER introduces a neuro-symbolic approach to continuous-time dynamic graph forecasting that uses grounded temporal facts and executable rules. This aligns with MIMIC's focus on neuro-symbolic agent models and the analysis of societal-scale interactions.

card.one_liner: LiFTER is a neuro-symbolic predictor for continuous-time dynamic graphs that turns link forecasting into verifiable grounded computations.
card.key_idea: It represents interactions as grounded facts and executes a finite language of temporal rules (bindings, renewal, position, transitions) to compute signed contributions to the logit.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four CTDG benchmarks (Wikipedia, Reddit, MOOC, LastFM) against neural baselines; achieved competitive forecasting and superior explanation accuracy and deletion fidelity.
card.limitation: Performance on random-negative forecasting is lower than neural baselines, particularly on LastFM, as it relies on grounded historical evidence.
